idea-plugin.name: Vestige - Temporal Code Intelligence
idea-plugin.description:
Know what you're about to break.

Vestige reads your local git history and answers the questions that matter right before you change code: what else changes with this file, who actually knows it, and what already constrains it.

Everything runs on your own machine against your own git history. No account, no sign-in, no telemetry.

What it does
  • Files that change together. History shows which files keep getting committed alongside the one you're editing, with the shared-commit count so you can judge it yourself. Co-change analysis is well established in research but almost nowhere in an editor.
  • Who to ask. If you're changing a file you have little history with, Vestige names the person who has most of it. The count of low-history contributors is the ownership signal with the strongest empirical support for predicting defects.
  • History of a selection. Select some lines and see how those lines got that way, not just who touched them last.
  • CODEOWNERS that tells the truth. Nothing validates that file. Vestige checks it against real history and reports owners who never committed, owners who have left, and lines the platform silently skips.
  • Recovering deleted code. Browse and restore files deleted from the repository, well beyond Local History's window.
  • Decisions in context. Architectural decision records surfaced against the code they constrain.
Honest about its numbers
  • The debt score ranks files within one repository. It is never shown as money or hours — converting an arbitrary score into a currency figure produces a confident number with nothing behind it.
  • Co-change is a suggestion, not a gate. It is shown with its evidence so you can disagree with it.
  • There is no leaderboard and no per-person productivity metric. Vestige reports facts about the codebase, not about people.
  • AI features are optional and off-limits when disabled: setting Disable AI makes those paths unreachable, not merely idle. Answers are always shown next to the commits they were drawn from.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 1.1.0 — Freeze fix, honest metrics, new analysis
  • Fixed the IDE freezes. The real cause was uncancellable work holding the read lock: a keystroke needs the write lock and waits for every read action to release, which only happens at a cancellation check. The plugin had three. The dominant cost was a duplicate-code scan that compared every extracted pattern against every line window of every other file while recompiling its regexes in the inner loop; it is now an indexed clone detector. Two more paths ran a full tree diff for every commit pair on every tab switch and every save, and the health dashboard issued roughly 250 git calls from a panel constructor.
  • Cancellation throughout. Every file, commit and line loop now polls for cancellation, and ProcessCanceledException is rethrown rather than swallowed. History walks, project scans and snapshot storage are all bounded.
  • No more periodic re-analysis. Cache validity is keyed on the file's modification stamp instead of wall-clock age, so an idle IDE no longer re-analyses on a timer.
  • New: files that change together, with the shared-commit count as evidence.
  • New: history of the selected lines, answering how a block got that way rather than who touched it last.
  • New: CODEOWNERS audit — reports owners who never committed, owners inactive for six months, and lines the platform silently ignores.
  • New: who to ask — surfaces low-history contributors and names the file's main author, replacing the bus-factor score.
  • Removed the leaderboard. Ranking colleagues on git-derived statistics is not something this plugin should do.
  • Removed invented numbers. The "estimated remediation cost" was a score multiplied by a hardcoded hourly rate; a dashboard percentage and a "from last week" trend had no data behind them at all. All are gone.
  • Interface rebuilt. Panels now follow the IDE's own theme and fonts rather than a hardcoded dark palette that was unreadable on light themes, and the tool window builds one panel on open instead of eleven.
  • Removed dead subsystems that were unreachable, including one containing unbounded recursion.
Version 1.0.6.2
  • Bounded the analysis cache and made listener handling thread-safe. Note: this release's notes claimed to have resolved the UI freezes; it did not — the blocking work was untouched. That is fixed in 1.1.0.
Version 1.0.6.1
  • Asynchronous analysis engine, JCEF dashboard, local snapshot history, folder-level heatmaps.
Version 1.0.6
  • Marketplace icon, fixed an InstantiationException in the debt calculator, project view badges.
